papers.title: The Self-Importance of Moral Identity
papers.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces the moral identity scale measuring internalization and symbolization dimensions of moral self-concept. Shows that moral identity predicts moral behavior above and beyond moral reasoning.

papers.title: The Problem of Abortion and the Doctrine of the Double Effect
papers.abstract_snippet: Introduces the trolley problem thought experiment to illustrate the doctrine of double effect, laying the groundwork for decades of moral psychology research on the distinction between doing and allowing harm.

papers.title: The Trolley Problem
papers.abstract_snippet: Extends Foot's trolley problem with additional variants including the footbridge case, establishing the canonical set of trolley dilemmas used in moral psychology research.

papers.title: Moral Machine on LLMs
papers.abstract_snippet: Applies the Moral Machine experimental paradigm to large language models, comparing LLM trolley problem responses to the cross-cultural human data from the original experiment.

papers.title: How Can a Deontological Decision Lead to Moral Satisfaction? The Role of Moral Identity
papers.authors: Xu, Z. X. & Ma, H. K.
papers.abstract_snippet: Examines how moral identity mediates the relationship between deontological decision-making and moral satisfaction in a Chinese cultural context, extending moral identity research cross-culturally.

papers.title: Moral Identity and Psychological Distance: The Case of Adolescent Volunteering
papers.authors: Hardy, S. A., Bhattacharjee, A., Reed, A., & Aquino, K.
papers.abstract_snippet: Explores the relationship between moral identity and psychological distance in adolescents, showing that moral identity centrality predicts prosocial behavior even toward psychologically distant others.

papers.title: Moral Identity and the Expanding Circle of Moral Regard Toward Out-Groups
papers.venue: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology
papers.abstract_snippet: Shows that moral identity predicts the expansion of moral regard toward out-groups, with individuals high in moral identity internalization showing greater concern for out-group welfare.

papers.title: The Moral Machine Experiment
papers.authors: Awad, E., Dsouza, S., Shariff, A., Rahwan, I., & Bonnefon, J.-F.
papers.abstract_snippet: Massive cross-cultural study of moral preferences in autonomous vehicle trolley-type dilemmas, providing the canonical dataset of human trolley problem responses.

papers.title: The Role of Conscious Reasoning and Intuition in Moral Judgment: Testing Three Principles of Harm
papers.authors: Cushman, F., Young, L., & Hauser, M.
papers.abstract_snippet: Tests three principles underlying moral judgments about harm in trolley-type scenarios: action, intention, and contact principles. Shows intuitive application of these principles even without conscious awareness.
